title: Integrate Smart Routing with burst admission decisions (deterministic deny/fallback/backpressure)
creator: Mina Haddad
content:
Goal
Integrate the routing/gateway path with the Burst Admission Controller so that:
- burst-capable Dedicated tenants can temporarily exceed baseline capacity when admitted
- denials are handled gracefully (backpressure / fallback / clear error semantics)
- decisions remain deterministic and debuggable (no “heisenbugs” due to telemetry jitter)

Context / links
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-burst-capacity-prd.json
- Design spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/burst-pool-architecture-and-guardrails.json
- ADR (semantics): confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-burst-pool-admission-control-semantics.json
- ADR (fairness): confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-fairness-model-for-shared-burst-pools.json
- Admission controller service doc: confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/burst-admission-controller-service.json
- Denial reason codes (support): ENG-4881
- Related PRs (implementation)
  - PR-23795 add denial reason codes and client surface
  - PR-23810 integrate routing with burst admission decisions

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Implementing the fairness algorithm itself (ENG-4821)
- Metering/billing export (ENG-4827)
- Console UX (ENG-4855)

Acceptance criteria
1) Routing calls admission controller only when a request would exceed reserved baseline and tenant has burst enabled.
2) Denial behavior is deterministic for a request across retries within a bounded window (see “Determinism” below).
3) Denials are surfaced with standardized reason codes + retry hints; routing does not silently spin/retry.
4) Fallback behavior is explicit and safe:
   - never route a Dedicated request to shared Hosted by default
   - only fallback to a pre-configured compatible variant within the same tenant’s Dedicated footprint (e.g., lower context variant) when policy allows
5) Clear operational signals:
   - routing emits metrics for admit/deny results, reason codes, and time spent waiting (if queued)
   - logs include a redacted “decision explanation id” that Support can use with internal debug tooling
6) Feature-flagged and kill-switchable by region + hardware class + tenant.

Proposed routing flow (data plane)
High-level steps for each request:
A. Identify tenant + route (Dedicated cluster, region, hw class) via existing Smart Routing selection.
B. Determine whether the request is “baseline” or “burst candidate”:
   - baseline if reserved capacity tokens/slots available per the local capacity tracker
   - burst candidate if baseline tracker indicates saturation AND tenant has burst enabled AND request is eligible (no policy violations)
C. For burst candidates, call Admission Controller:
   - request includes: tenant_id, route_id, region, hw_class, requested_units (normalized), priority_tier, request_id, idempotency_key
   - response includes: admit/deny, reason_code, decision_ttl_ms, retry_after_ms (optional), admitted_units (optional)
D. If admitted: proceed with routing to the burst pool attachment for that route.
E. If denied:
   - if deny type is “soft” (retryable): return 429 with reason code + Retry-After (or optionally enqueue if configured)
   - if deny type is “hard” (non-retryable policy): return 403/409 equivalent error class (per API contract) with reason code
   - if fallback policy exists: evaluate deterministic fallback (see below) and either route to fallback or deny

Determinism requirements
We saw in early staging tests that non-deterministic deny/admit across client retries created confusing customer behavior and made Support triage nearly impossible.

This ticket enforces:
- A stable request identity:
  - routing generates/request-passes an idempotency_key (prefer client-provided, otherwise derived from request_id + connection/session)
  - admission controller uses idempotency_key + decision_ttl_ms to return consistent decisions across a short window
- A stable policy evaluation snapshot:
  - routing passes a “capacity_epoch” token when available from fleet telemetry; if absent, admission controller uses its latest epoch and returns it in the decision explanation
- No hidden client-side jitter:
  - routing does not automatically retry admission calls except on transport failures (bounded, 1 retry max) and only if idempotency_key is preserved

Denial handling semantics
We implement the following mapping in routing:
- BURST_DISABLED / TENANT_NOT_ELIGIBLE: immediate deny (non-retryable) with clear message; suggests contacting support/sales
- COOLDOWN_ACTIVE: deny retryable with Retry-After = remaining cooldown
- TENANT_BURST_CAP_REACHED: deny retryable, Retry-After = policy-defined backoff (or provided by admission)
- POOL_SATURATED / FLEET_SAFETY_CAP: deny retryable, with short Retry-After; include “global safety” hint
- TELEMETRY_LAG_PROTECTION: deny retryable, Retry-After short; log annotation so SRE can correlate to telemetry health

API/error surface
- For gateway / SDK-facing APIs: return 429 Too Many Requests for retryable denials, include:
  - x-redwood-burst-denial-reason: <REASON_CODE>
  - retry-after: <seconds> when applicable
  - x-redwood-decision-id: <opaque id>
- For non-retryable denials: return 403 (feature not enabled / policy) or 409 (conflict with route/policy) depending on existing Redwood error conventions.
- Body includes a stable message template for Support macros (ENG-4881 will maintain canonical wording).

Fallback rules (explicit, conservative)
Default: no fallback.
Optional (tenant-configured): allow fallback to a compatible route/model variant only if:
- same tenant, same region
- explicitly configured in control plane (ENG-4816)
- “fallback_eligible” signal from policy engine is true
- determinism: for a given idempotency_key, we choose the same fallback route consistently for decision_ttl_ms

Observability
Add/confirm the following metrics at routing level (names aligned with burst metrics taxonomy draft):
- routing_burst_admission_requests_total{region, hw_class, tenant_tier}
- routing_burst_admission_denials_total{reason_code,...}
- routing_burst_admission_latency_ms (p50/p95)
- routing_burst_fallbacks_total{fallback_route}

Also:
- structured log fields: tenant_id (hashed), route_id, reason_code, decision_id, capacity_epoch
- dashboard links to be added in ENG-4833; this ticket ensures the signals exist and are low-cardinality.

Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - reason code mapping to status codes + headers
  - determinism across retries given same idempotency_key within TTL
  - fallback selection determinism
- Integration tests (with admission controller stubbed):
  - baseline saturation triggers admission call
  - deny -> 429 with Retry-After, no internal retries
  - telemetry lag mode triggers TELEMETRY_LAG_PROTECTION and correct behavior
- Load tests (ENG-4841 owns harness): ensure no routing regressions for non-burst tenants; verify tail latency not amplified due to synchronous admission calls (timeouts + circuit breaker)

Timeouts / circuit breakers
- Admission controller call timeout: 30ms default (configurable), with per-region overrides
- On admission controller timeout/unavailable:
  - treat as deny retryable with reason_code=ADMISSION_UNAVAILABLE
  - do not attempt to “optimistically admit” (safety first)
- Routing should respect global circuit breaker flag (ENG-4902 / PR-23919) that forces deny for burst even if tenant eligible.

Rollout
- Feature flags:
  - burst_admission_integration_enabled (global)
  - burst_admission_enabled_regions (allowlist)
  - burst_admission_enabled_hw_classes (allowlist)
  - tenant.burst.enabled (control plane)
- Staged rollout:
  1) staging + synthetic load
  2) internal dogfood tenants
  3) 1-2 beta customers per region/hw
  4) expand allowlist

Progress / updates
2025-03-06 (Elena): Started implementation behind feature flag. Working with Ethan on admission request schema; aligning on idempotency_key + decision_ttl.
2025-03-11 (Ravi): Requested explicit mapping of reason_code -> HTTP status + Retry-After. Added requirement that routing never silently retries admission beyond 1 transport retry.
2025-03-14 (Peter Holtz): Please ensure admission call is guarded by routing-level circuit breaker; timeouts must fail closed (deny) to protect fleet.
2025-03-20 (Elena): Implemented deterministic fallback selection (config-gated). Added unit tests for stable selection by idempotency_key.
2025-03-27 (Mina): Reviewed behavior with Support: ensure headers include reason code and decision id; align message templates with ENG-4881.
2025-04-03 (Elena): Opened PR-23810. Added metrics + low-cardinality labels. Added log redaction for tenant_id.
2025-04-10 (Allison Grant): Metrics look good; remove route_id label from denial totals (too high cardinality). Keep route_id only in logs.
2025-04-15 (Elena): Updated per observability feedback; added docstring comments for reason codes and retry guidance.
2025-04-18: Merged PR-23810. Marking ticket Done.

Deliverables
- Code merged: routing path calls admission controller for burst candidates; handles admit/deny with deterministic semantics
- Metrics + logs: added and validated in staging
- Feature-flagged rollout gates in place (coordinated with ENG-4848)

Open follow-ups
- ENG-4881: finalize Support macros + public docs for denial reason codes (routing now emits the needed headers)
- ENG-4841: validate tail latency impact under burst spikes; adjust admission timeout if needed
- ENG-4902: ensure global circuit breaker policy is surfaced to routing consistently across regions

Notes
Key principle: fail closed for burst (deny) to protect platform SLOs. Customers can always increase baseline reservations for guaranteed throughput; burst is opportunistic by design, and routing should be transparent about that via reason codes + retry hints.
